$comment: GOL-866 / GOL-864 §1 performance budget. Byte budgets are gzip-transferred unless noted. 1 KB = 1024 B. Edit here, not in the scripts — scripts/perf-budget.mjs and scripts/css-component-budget.mjs both read this file.

route.$comment: Per-route budget from GOL-864 §1b. Measured off each app's built .next/ manifests (the same chunk data @next/bundle-analyzer visualizes). JS = first-load JS (shared runtime + route chunks), CSS = route stylesheets, both gzipped.

js.$comment: budget 150 KB (warn), ceiling 400 KB (error) — the outer limit for heavy interactive routes.

css.$comment: 60 KB per route (error). Tailwind is purged; a route over this signals un-purged or one-off CSS.

componentCss.$comment: GOL-864 §1c per-component CSS ceiling — the Angular `budgets` analog. Targets bespoke component stylesheets in @grove/ui, where drift and bloat accumulate. App globals.css, generated ds-theme.*.css, and token contract.css are app-wide/generated, not per-component, so they are excluded. Sizes are UNCOMPRESSED bytes.

baseline.$comment: Ratchet: files already over the 6 KB ceiling when this gate landed (GOL-866). Each is grandfathered at its recorded size — it may only SHRINK, never grow, and new files get the strict 6 KB ceiling. Refactor tracked in the GOL-866 follow-up child issue; drop an entry here once its file is back under 6 KB. Regenerate with: node scripts/css-component-budget.mjs --update-baseline

lighthouse.$comment: GOL-864 §1a lab targets + §1b total weight. Enforced by lighthouserc.json against a preview URL. INP is a field-only metric (no lab equivalent), so total-blocking-time is the lab proxy documented in the perf standards doc.
